question.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-4,3,-1)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨6,-1,5⟩)\cdot ⟨-1,2,-2⟩=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(6,-1,5).$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨6,-1,5⟩-⟨-4,3,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨10,-4,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-1,2,-2⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|10\cdot (-1)+(-4)\cdot 2+6\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-10-8-12|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|-30|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{30}{3} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
